subsystems.name: Prospecting and mining units
subsystems.role: find and extract usable material — regolith, ice, metal-bearing rock — without human crews.

subsystems.name: Material refinery
subsystems.role: turn raw dug material into usable feedstock.
parts: electrolysis or reduction cells to free metals and oxygen

subsystems.name: Fabrication line
subsystems.role: make parts from that feedstock rather than shipping them from Earth.

subsystems.name: Assemblers
subsystems.role: position, join and test new machines, including copies of themselves.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal
subsystems.role: keep the whole loop running day and night, in vacuum and extreme temperatures.
parts: solar arrays or small fission reactor

subsystems.name: Swarm control
subsystems.role: coordinate thousands of units toward one structure without a human directing each one.

buildSteps.title: Deliver a seed factory
buildSteps.detail: Launch a compact starter kit of machines — a mining unit, a refinery, a printer and a few assemblers — since no design starts fully self-replicating.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop on simple mass
buildSteps.detail: Measure the closure fraction: what share of the factory's mass, by part type, can be made from local material. Start with structural beams, panels and fasteners.

buildSteps.title: Extract feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Mine regolith or rock, reduce oxides to get metals and oxygen, and mill the output into powder and wire the printers can use.

buildSteps.title: Print and machine parts
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate the simple, bulky components locally, while continuing to import the hard ones — chips, bearings, motors, seals — from Earth.

buildSteps.title: Assemble a copy
buildSteps.detail: Robots build a second set of machines from those parts, using their own arms and the same jigs they were made with. This step, not the printing, is the hard one.

buildSteps.title: Raise the closure fraction by generation
buildSteps.detail: Each generation makes a slightly larger share of itself; the goal is to shrink the imported 'vitamin' list toward nothing.

buildSteps.title: Scale the swarm
buildSteps.detail: Once copies can be made, unit count grows on a doubling curve, and control software partitions work across the whole population.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the megastructure
buildSteps.detail: The swarm converges on the target — a large solar array, a habitat, a radio telescope dish — building it in parallel from many small robots.

buildSteps.title: Inspect, repair, retire
buildSteps.detail: Autonomous inspection and self-repair keep the population working; failed units are recycled back into feedstock.

prerequisites.why: von Neumann's universal-constructor work in the mid-20th century set out what replication logically requires; NASA's 1980 summer study on advanced space automation sketched a self-replicating lunar factory.
small-scale extraction has been demonstrated in labs and on Mars, but not as an industrial supply chain.
regolith and metal powders can be sintered or melted into parts, but strength, tolerance and repeatability are far below aerospace standards.
swarms of tens to hundreds have been demonstrated; thousands of units operating for years without intervention is untested.
the computing and motor components are exactly the parts hardest to make off-Earth, and the ones most likely to fail.
a seed factory only pays off if its mass is small and its delivery cheap.

pathway.milestone: terrestrial testbeds where robot teams mine, refine and print simple parts
pathway.unlocks: data on closure fractions and failure modes.

pathway.milestone: a robotic outpost that makes structural elements and oxygen from local rock
pathway.unlocks: parts of a base built without launching every kilogram.

pathway.milestone: a factory that builds a meaningful share of its own replacement parts
pathway.unlocks: growth limited by manufacturing rate rather than launch cadence.

pathway.milestone: supervised replication at scale, building large orbital or lunar structures
pathway.unlocks: megastructures whose mass never has to leave Earth — contingent on solving electronics, control and safe replication limits.
